name: Kuranda Scenic Railway
label: Kuranda Railway
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Freshwater Station' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Freshwater Railway Station' (way/290473283): middle (40 m across); moved 5 m off buildings.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap relation/2632233: large area 'Kuranda Scenic Railway' (18521 m across): previous pin kept, it lies inside.
notes: Historic rainforest railway, photographed here at Freshwater station.

text.description:
The Kuranda Scenic Railway is a heritage-listed line that climbs from Cairns up the Great Dividing Range to the town of Kuranda. Work began in 1886 and passenger services started on 25 June 1891. Builders cut 15 hand-made tunnels and built 37 bridges to lift the track from sea level to 328 metres. The whole line is 37 km long, and a one-way trip takes about one hour and 55 minutes.

For a phone photo, the easiest place to start is Freshwater Station at the foot of the range. The old station buildings, the carriages and the locomotive all sit together, with green hills behind. It is a simple, friendly scene, and the train gives you a strong subject whether it is standing or pulling away. The station also has an information centre, a gift shop and a café in an old train carriage, so there is plenty to look at while you wait.

Stand on the platform, roughly beside the carriages where the train leaves for Kuranda. Try one wide shot of the whole train with the hills behind, then move closer for details such as the carriage doors, the locomotive and the station signs. If you ride up, Barron Falls Station is a second photo stop. From its platform you see Barron Falls dropping over the rock cliffs across the gorge, with the heritage train beside you. Stoney Creek Falls is best photographed from inside the train.
text.geographic_location: The railway runs through the northern suburbs of Cairns, including Stratford, Freshwater and Redlynch, before it climbs the Macalister Range.
text.directions_text: The map shows no nearby station or tram stop, so start from Cairns city centre and check local transport options for getting to the suburb of Freshwater. Trains can be boarded at Freshwater Station, so check which departure station your service uses. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the default lens (1x) for the carriages and station buildings together. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if the platform is narrow and you want the whole length of the train. Use 2x telephoto, if your phone has it, for the locomotive and small details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (the platform, roughly beside the carriages where the train departs for Kuranda). The train with its carriages and locomotive leaving the historic station platform, with the surrounding hills behind.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and line the carriages up along one of the horizontal lines, so the train looks straight. Keep the hills as a green band behind it. Take a second shot closer in on the locomotive or a carriage door. If you ride up, Barron Falls Station is a good alternative: from its platform you can shoot the falls across the gorge with the train standing beside you. Stay on the platform and behind the barriers there.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the train to focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright, so the carriage colours stay rich. Try a Live Photo as the train pulls out, but hold the phone steady.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Choose a departure time and arrive a little early, so you can take photos before boarding. For Barron Falls, the falls flow strongest after rain, so January to February is better than the drier months. Only some services stop at Barron Falls Station, so check your timetable.

text.access_note: Barron Falls Station can only be reached by riding the train, so check the official site and your timetable before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Arriving early before a departure gives time to take photos on the platform before boarding.
Lowering the exposure slider helps keep colours rich when the sky is bright.
Live Photos can capture the train pulling out if the phone is held steady.

name: Cairns Esplanade Lagoon
label: Esplanade Lagoon
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Fogarty Park' (1 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Fogarty Park' (way/219741174): middle (264 m across).
pin_note: Position from OSM W55293523 (Cairns Esplanade Lagoon): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Free saltwater swimming lagoon on the waterfront.

text.description: Cairns Esplanade Lagoon sits on the city's waterfront, with the sea beyond it and the town behind. It photographs well because several things line up in one frame: still water, palms, the fish sculptures and the skyline. From here the lagoon and waterfront sit against the city skyline, which gives a different view from the one at the water's edge. If you also want the classic close-up, walk down to the lagoon afterwards. There the water fills the foreground, the ocean sits behind it, and the fish sculptures and palms frame the scene. Coconut Grove is a third option. It is a palm-lined walkway along the Esplanade, good for framing sky and sea rather than the lagoon. The best moment varies. Some favour the lagoon at high tide, others sunrise along the boardwalk, so it is worth taking a few frames at different times if you are staying nearby. Keep your phone level and use the gridlines so the waterline stays straight. Look for people, palms or sculptures to put in the foreground, which makes the scene feel bigger. Check current opening hours before you go. Drones are typically restricted near the lagoon, so check local rules if you travel with one.
text.geographic_location: On the Esplanade waterfront in central Cairns, about 210 m north-west of the stand-here point in Fogarty Park, with the city skyline behind.
text.directions_text: No public transport is listed for this spot, so start from Cairns city centre and walk to the Esplanade and Fogarty Park. Check current opening hours before you go. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the lagoon against the skyline. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want more water and sky, and use 2x if your phone has it to pick out the buildings behind.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Fogarty Park. The lagoon and waterfront set against the city skyline behind it. The lagoon itself lies to the north-west.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put the water and waterfront in the lower third and let the skyline fill the middle, using the gridlines to keep the horizon level. For an alternative, walk to the lagoon's edge and shoot across the water with the ocean behind and the fish sculptures and palms framing the scene. Coconut Grove, the palm-lined walkway, gives a frame of sky and sea.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the skyline to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky keeps its colour. If the water is moving, try a Live Photo and pick the best frame afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Some favour the lagoon at high tide, others sunrise on the boardwalk. Early morning is a sensible first try, but check tide times if you want high water.

text.access_note: Fogarty Park and the waterfront are public areas, but check the lagoon's current opening hours before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Fogarty Park is a short walk south-east of the lagoon and close to the Esplanade.
Early morning is a sensible first time to try for softer light and fewer people.
Dragging the exposure slider down helps keep the sky's colour.
The lagoon is a public water space beside the sea.

name: Cairns Aquarium
label: Cairns Aquarium
camera_source: No separate stand-here point: photographed at the spot itself (indoors, from its top, or right in front of it); drawn as the split pin.
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q50822227: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Aquarium showing Great Barrier Reef and rainforest habitats.

text.description: Cairns Aquarium is a public aquarium in Cairns, Queensland that opened in 2017. It is a three-level building holding 71 tanks and more than 15,000 animals, shown in 10 different habitats, from rainforest streams and mangroves to the Great Barrier Reef and the Coral Sea. For a visitor with a phone, the big tanks are the draw: the Coral Sea Oceanarium has sharks, rays and large reef fish, and the Billabong Amphitheatre is Australia's largest freshwater tank at 400,000 litres. The building also houses a turtle rehabilitation centre where rescued sea turtles are cared for before release. It photographs well because the animals are large and slow-moving, and the tanks give a steady blue backdrop that makes a clear subject easy to pick out. The outside of the building is a simple, easy shot to show where you were, while the real pictures are taken indoors, so allow time to wander. Indoors, light is low and the glass is reflective, so press the phone close to the glass, or shade it with your hand, to cut out reflections. Wait for a shark or ray to swim towards you rather than chasing it. Keep your screen brightness up so you can judge the exposure. Some exhibits hold replicas rather than live animals, such as the deep-sea fish and the fossils, so they make calm, still subjects. Check the official site before you go for current entry details.
text.geographic_location: Cairns Aquarium is in Cairns, Queensland, Australia. A restaurant next to the aquarium has a viewing tank looking out under a jetty.
text.directions_text: No train or tram stops are listed for this spot. The phone icon on the map is the aquarium itself, so the building is right where you are standing. Head to the aquarium and check the official site before you go for the current entrance arrangements. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the default lens (1x) for most tank shots, and switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) in front of the largest tanks to take in the whole scene. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for a single fish or ray when you cannot get close to the glass.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Once inside, stand close in front of the glass of the big tanks, as the subject here is the building and its exhibits all around you.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and place a shark or ray on one of the lines with some empty blue water in front of its nose. Hold the phone flat against the glass, or shade it with your free hand, to reduce reflections. For a wider view of a big tank, try the ultra-wide (0.5x) from a few steps back.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap to focus on the animal and then slide the exposure down a little so the water does not turn grey or washed out. Try a Live Photo for a swimming animal, so you can pick the best frame afterwards. Avoid flash, as it bounces off the glass.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Dark rooms and tank lighting are the same all day, so time matters little for indoor pictures. Choose a quieter moment if you can, as it is easier to get a clear spot at the glass; for any outside shot of the building, daylight is easiest.

text.access_note: The turtle centre tours cost extra, so check the official site for details.

name: Cairns Night Markets
label: Night Markets
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Cairns Night Markets' (2 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from OSM N4230048191 (Cairns Night Markets): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Popular evening souvenir market on the Esplanade.

text.description:
Cairns Night Markets is a covered market where the photography is all about the evening atmosphere. Once the lights come on, the stalls glow, the food court adds warm colour, and the crowd drifting between souvenir tables gives you plenty of candid, street-style scenes. The market is fully undercover, so it gives shelter from rain or sun.

There is no outdoor viewpoint for the market's exterior, so the phone icon on the map sits inside the market itself, along the stall lanes. Walk the lanes slowly and look for rows of lit stalls, colourful souvenir displays and the busy glow around the food court. Entrances are at 73-75 Esplanade and on Abbott Street, so you can loop through from one to the other.

Photo guides say the market looks best in the evening after dark, once the lights are on. One also mentions the golden hour just before sunset as a pleasant time to arrive. Photography is generally fine for personal use, but be polite to stallholders and ask permission before taking close-up photos of people.
text.geographic_location: Cairns Night Markets has entrances at 73-75 Esplanade and on Abbott Street, Cairns.
text.directions_text: Head for the Esplanade in Cairns. There are entrances at 73-75 Esplanade and on Abbott Street. Once inside, the phone icon on the map is along the stall lanes. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for stalls and the lit food court. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) in the wider lanes to fit in rows of stalls and the crowd. Use telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for details on souvenir tables or for candid shots from a polite distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. From here the photo shows the lit stalls and the busy evening crowd under the covered roof, with the glow of the food court nearby.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up a lane so the rows of stalls lead towards the middle of the frame. Put a lit stall or a colourful display in the foreground and let the crowd fill the background. Wait for a gap in the crowd, or let people walk through the frame for a street-style feel. Ask before taking close-up photos of people.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap to focus on a lit stall, then drag the exposure slider down a little so bright lights do not wash out. In dimmer corners, use night mode and hold the phone steady against your body or a rail. Ask people to stay still for a moment, as night mode can blur anyone who moves. Live Photos can capture the movement of the crowd.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Evening after dark, when the lights are on. One guide also suggests golden hour just before sunset.

text.access_note: Entry is described as free, but access and opening times can change, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Bright stall lighting can make a phone overexpose, so lowering the exposure slider helps.
Night mode can blur people who are moving.

name: Flecker Botanical Gardens
label: Botanic Gardens
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Centenary Lakes' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Centenary Lakes Nature Play' (way/1459997244): middle (90 m across).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/211472097: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Flecker Garden' (279 m across).
notes: Tropical gardens with orchids and rainforest walks.

text.description:
Flecker Botanical Gardens, now known as Cairns Botanic Gardens, is a heritage-listed public garden on Collins Avenue in Edge Hill. It began in the mid-1880s as part of a recreation reserve, only about ten years after Cairns was first surveyed. Over the decades it grew through the work of the botanist Eugene Fitzalan, council nurserymen and, from the 1930s to the 1950s, the naturalist Dr Hugo Flecker. It was declared a permanent recreation reserve of about 44 hectares in 1921 and was added to the Queensland Heritage Register in 2007.

For a phone photographer the pleasure is in the variety. Lush tropical planting, open lawn and still water all sit close together. The best-suited view here is Centenary Lakes. It is a freshwater lake with a Chinese friendship garden beside it, and the water gives you soft reflections of the surrounding plants, which look especially good towards sunset. Back in the main garden, the Watkins Munro Martin Conservatory looks good from the big front lawn, with the old Teak tree in the foreground. The Munro-Martin Fernery, with its shade-cloth walls, can be photographed across the same open lawn.

Centenary Lakes is a separate section reached by a boardwalk across Collins Avenue, so allow extra time and don't try to fit everything into a quick stop. Check the official site for opening hours and any access changes before you go, especially if you are planning a sunset visit.
text.geographic_location: The gardens are in the Edge Hill district of Cairns, along Collins Avenue, on the southern side of Mt Islay in the foothills of the Mt Whitfield Range. The garden area is bounded by Collins Avenue and McCormack, Goodwin and McDonnell Streets.
text.directions_text: No public transport stop is listed nearby, so head for Collins Avenue in Edge Hill. The boardwalk across Collins Avenue links the two sections. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for reflections, as it keeps the water and plants looking natural. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in more of the lake edge, or use 2x to pick out a single plant or its reflection.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Centenary Lakes (lake edge, with the Chinese friendship garden nearby). Water reflections of the lake and surrounding garden plants, which suit a sunset shot. From here you are looking across the water at the lake and the garden plants around it, with their reflections on the surface. The main garden and its lawn lie to the north-west.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the water's edge on the lower third line, so the reflections fill the frame. Keep the phone level so the horizon stays straight. As an alternative, from the front lawn in the main garden you can frame the Watkins Munro Martin Conservatory with the old Teak tree in the foreground, or the Munro-Martin Fernery across the open lawn.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the brightest part of the sky or water to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the sunset colours don't wash out. Wait until the water is calm before shooting. If you take a few frames, a Live Photo can help you pick the one with the clearest reflection.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Around sunset, when the lake reflections are at their best. Check the opening hours before a late visit.

text.access_note: The gardens are a public park, but check the official site before you go for opening hours and any access changes.

name: Cairns Convention Centre
label: Convention Centre
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Wharf Street' (2 web pages); placed at the stretch of Wharf Street nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q5017709: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.

text.description: The Cairns Convention Centre is the city's big venue for conferences, concerts and basketball, and its frontage is the part visitors will want to photograph. The building covers about 31,000 square metres on a 2.2-hectare site in the city centre. Stage one opened on 26 June 1996, and it was described as Australia's first regional convention centre and the country's first environmentally designed public building. It is also the home court of the Cairns Taipans basketball team. A straight-on view works well because the entrance and the building's broad shape fit in one frame, with people and signs giving a sense of scale. For a different mood, the Cairns Esplanade offers a waterfront view of the centre from the promenade, with the harbour and palms. An expansion adding meeting space and a third level was planned, so the building may look different from older photos. Keep to the pavement and watch for traffic and people arriving for events.
text.geographic_location: In Cairns City (the CBD), on Wharf Street, close to Trinity Inlet and the Esplanade waterfront.
text.directions_text: Start from the Cairns city centre and come on foot from the CBD. The centre is on Wharf Street. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural straight-on view of the entrance. If the facade will not fit from the pavement, switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x). Use 2x or the telephoto lens for signs and architectural details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Wharf Street (frontage facing the main entrance). The main entrance and facade of the centre, seen straight on from the street.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line the building's horizontal edges up with them so the facade does not lean. Hold the phone level and keep the entrance in the middle of the frame. With the ultra-wide, avoid tilting upwards, as it stretches the edges of the building. For a second option, take a waterfront shot of the centre from the Cairns Esplanade, with the harbour and palms in view.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the facade to set focus and exposure, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright and washing out the building. Take a few shots in case people walk into the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Choose a time when the sun is not directly behind the entrance, often early morning or late afternoon; check where the light falls when you arrive. Quieter times between events make it easier to get a clear view.

text.access_note: The frontage can be photographed from the public street, but entry to the venue depends on events, so check the official site before you go.

name: Cairns Wharf Complex
label: Cairns Wharf
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Wharf Street' (2 web pages); placed at the stretch of Wharf Street nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q24190724: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Departure point for Great Barrier Reef boat trips.

text.description: Cairns Wharf Complex is the old working waterfront of the city, built in stages between 1910 and 1948 and added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 17 December 1999. Concrete wharves with long sheds on top replaced earlier timber jetties. The first wharf, at the end of Lake Street, was finished by 1912, and Cairns was the first Queensland port to use reinforced concrete wharves to any real extent. A striking clock tower was added above the number 3 shed in 1948. That shed has since been reused as the Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal. The complex photographs well because of its long, repeating roofline, the clock tower rising above it, and the way the city streets run down towards Trinity Inlet. For a street-level view, stand on Wharf Street, on the stretch running down to the complex's number 2 gate, and look east. The sheds and gateway sit in the middle of the frame, with the streets leading towards the water. If you want a different angle, the north end of Trinity Wharf puts moored yachts in the foreground with the sheds and inlet behind. The corner of Abbott Street and Lake Street gives a longer view of the four-faced clock tower. Keep your phone level so the long sheds do not lean, and take a few frames at different distances.
text.geographic_location: In Cairns City, along Wharf Street beside Trinity Inlet, with the old wharves running along the waterfront at the foot of Lake Street.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so start from the centre of Cairns City and head towards the waterfront at Trinity Inlet. Go to Wharf Street, which runs beside the complex. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the sheds and gateway as you see them. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want the full roofline or a close-up of the gate. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for the clock tower from further away.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Wharf Street (stretch running down to the complex's number 2 gate). A street-level view that frames the complex's sheds and gateway with the city streets leading down toward Trinity Inlet. From here you look east and the photo shows the sheds and gateway framed by the city streets leading down towards Trinity Inlet.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and line the street up with the centre of the frame so the sheds sit evenly on either side. Keep the phone level to stop the verticals leaning. Leave some sky above the roofline if the clock tower is in view. For an alternative, try Trinity Wharf at the north end for yachts in the foreground, or the corner of Abbott Street and Lake Street for a distance view of the clock tower.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the sheds to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky keeps its colour. If you want a person in the shot, try portrait mode with them standing a few steps in front of the gateway.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon or early morning are usually kinder than the harsh midday sun in Cairns. In the afternoon, looking east, the sun is behind you and lights the front of the sheds.

text.access_note: Wharf Street is a public street, but the wharf area and cruise terminal may have restricted access at times, so check the official site before you go.

name: Cairns railway station
label: Cairns Station
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Cairns Railway Station' (2 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q5017724: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Start of the Kuranda Scenic Railway.

text.description: Cairns railway station is the city's terminus for the line from Brisbane and the starting point for two tourist trains: the Kuranda Scenic Railway and the Savannahlander. It is a working station rather than a postcard building. It is built into the Cairns Central shopping centre, with the two platforms underneath the car park, so what you photograph is mostly the Bunda Street frontage and the everyday comings and goings around it. The railway story gives the picture some depth. The first station here opened in 1891 as a two-storey timber building with ornate verandahs. It was replaced in 1955 by a cream brick building, and the current station was opened on 7 May 1996 on the opposite side of the site. That means the building you see today is modern, not the old timber one, so don't go expecting Victorian verandahs. A good photo here is a simple, honest one: the station frontage with a little street life in front of it, to show where the Kuranda Scenic Railway and the Savannahlander begin. Stand back far enough on the footpath to include the whole entrance, and wait for a gap in the people passing. If you are riding the Kuranda Scenic Railway, a quick shot of the entrance before you board makes a nice start to your photo story. Keep the phone level so the building's vertical lines stay straight, and take a few frames, as the scene changes with each passing group.
text.geographic_location: In the Cairns CBD, on Bunda Street, built into the Cairns Central shopping centre.
text.directions_text: The station is in the middle of the Cairns CBD, joined to the Cairns Central shopping centre, so it is easy to find on foot from anywhere in the centre. If you are coming from further out, use the Cairns Central shopping centre as your landmark and look for the station entrance on Bunda Street. Platform 2 has a direct link to Bunda Street, and Platform 1 links to the shopping centre. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the frontage. If the pavement is narrow and you cannot step back far enough, switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the whole entrance in. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details such as signs and entrance features.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. The subject is the station itself, so there is no fixed viewing distance or direction. Find a spot on the Bunda Street footpath with a clear view of the frontage, check it on the ground, and step back far enough to frame the building.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and line the building up with them so the verticals stay straight. Leave a little pavement in the foreground and wait for people to clear or to walk through the scene. For variety, try one wide frame and one closer frame on the entrance.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the building to set focus, then slide the exposure down slightly if the sky is bright and the frontage goes dark. If you shoot inside the concourse or platform areas, which sit under the car park, try night mode for steadier, cleaner pictures; hold the phone still against a pillar or rail.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the frontage, and quieter moments between train departures make it easier to get a clear view.

text.access_note: The frontage is on a public footpath, but the platforms and train services are part of a working station and ticketed tourist railways, so check the official site before you go.

name: Hides Hotel
label: Hides Hotel
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Lake Street and Shields Street corner' (3 web pages); placed at crossing of Lake Street and Shields Street (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q24190586: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.

text.description:
Hides Hotel is a three-storey heritage hotel on the southern corner of Lake Street and Shields Street, in the middle of Cairns city. It was designed by the Cairns architect Sydenham Stanley Oxenham and built in 1928 in reinforced concrete, and the Shields Street side was completed by about 1936. When it went up it was one of the largest buildings in Cairns and one of only two with three storeys. It joined the Queensland Heritage Register in 1992.

It photographs well because the building has a clear, well-shaped corner. Wide timber verandahs run along both street frontages, and the second floor has arched windows with rendered mouldings. The words HIDES CAIRNS HOTEL run along the parapet on the Lake Street side, with a flagpole on a scrolled base above the central bay. That gives you a simple, readable subject: the verandahs, the lettering and the corner in one frame.

The present hotel stands beside the site of an earlier timber Hides' Cairns Hotel from 1885, which had double verandahs and an observation tower. That building is gone, but it is a nice detail to know when you are standing in front of its successor.

For your phone, step back as far as the pavement allows and keep the whole corner in the frame. Watch for people and traffic crossing the bottom of the shot, and wait a moment for a clear gap. Shields Street near the hotel is a pedestrian mall, so check for street works or events before you go.
text.geographic_location: Hides Hotel is in Cairns City, in the central business district, on the southern corner of Lake Street and Shields Street. Shields Street near the hotel is a pedestrian mall.

text.description:
Cairns School of Arts is a heritage-listed building that now houses the Cairns Museum, a local history museum run by the Cairns Historical Society. It stands at 93–105 Lake Street in the city centre. The two-storey building opened on 5 December 1907. It was designed by Tunbridge, Tunbridge & Lynch and includes an early use of reinforced concrete in Queensland. Later extensions ran the frontage along Lake Street, and the last one, in 1939–40, was in Art Deco style. It was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 21 October 1992.

It photographs well because the corner shows several layers of history in one frame: the older verandahed section, the decorative parapet, the lettering and the later Art Deco stretch. Stand at the south-western corner of Lake Street and Shields Street. From there you get the full corner facade framed by the junction. Keep your phone upright to fit both storeys, and use the gridlines so the verticals stay straight. If you want a quieter, more architectural picture, walk a little way along Shields Street. From there you can compare the 1907 heritage section with the modern museum addition. Traffic and pedestrians pass the corner, so wait for a gap and take a few frames.
text.geographic_location: In the centre of Cairns (Cairns City), on the corner of Lake Street and Shields Street.
text.directions_text: Walk from the centre of Cairns City to the corner of Lake Street and Shields Street. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the corner facade. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if pavement or traffic stops you stepping back far enough. Use telephoto (2x or more) for details such as the parapet and lettering.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand at the corner of Lake Street and Shields Street (south-western corner, the building's main corner facade). The full two-storey corner facade of the 1907 building with its verandahs, the date and the School of Arts lettering, framed by the intersection.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Use the gridlines and line up the building's vertical edges with them. Include both storeys and the verandahs, and leave a little pavement at the bottom. For a different view, walk along Shields Street, where the heritage 1907 section sits next to the contemporary museum addition.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the brightest part of the wall to focus, then lower the exposure slider slightly so the sky does not wash out and the lettering stays readable. Take a 0.5x shot and a 1x shot so you can choose later.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Check on site, as the front may be shaded or busy with pedestrians at some times.

text.access_note: The building is a working museum, so you can photograph the outside from the public street, but check the official Cairns Museum site before you go if you want to go inside.

text.description:
St Monica's Cathedral is the Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Cairns, and it is the only cathedral in the city. It was designed by the Brisbane architect Ian Ferrier and built in 1967–68 as a war memorial, dedicated to the Battle of the Coral Sea. It has been on the Queensland Heritage Register since 31 August 1998. Ferrier also designed the cathedrals in Darwin and Port Moresby.

It photographs well because the main door opens straight onto Abbott Street, so you can stand opposite and get the front of the building square-on. The cathedral sits among older church buildings, including the Old Cathedral, Bishop's House and St Joseph's Convent. Together they form a very intact group, so a slightly wider shot can show that this is a whole church precinct and not just one building.

For a simple, clean photo, stand on the street opposite the entrance, switch on the gridlines and line the doorway up with the centre of the frame. Keep the vertical lines straight by holding the phone upright and level. If you go inside, remember that it is a working church. Switch the flash off, keep your distance from anyone praying, and keep to the public areas. The stained-glass windows along the side and back walls are worth a few quiet shots if photography is allowed when you visit.
text.geographic_location: St Monica's Cathedral is on Abbott Street in Cairns City, in the central part of Cairns. It stands in a group of older church and convent buildings.
text.directions_text: Head for Abbott Street in the centre of Cairns City. The cathedral's main door faces Abbott Street. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the front. If the facade will not fit from across the street, switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x). A 2x telephoto setting is useful for the doorway and details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Abbott Street (opposite the main entrance, so the front facade faces you). The cathedral's front entrance and facade, framed from the street that the main door faces.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and place the main door on the centre line. Hold the phone upright and level so the walls do not lean. The ultra-wide lens can also include some of the surrounding gardens and neighbouring church buildings. For a different view, the stained-glass windows inside run floor to ceiling along the side and back walls, if photography is allowed when you visit.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the brightest part of the facade to focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the sky and pale walls keep their detail. Inside, keep the flash off and use night mode only if you can hold the phone very still.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the front of the building than the middle of the day.

text.access_note: This is an active place of worship, so respect services and worshippers, and check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements.

text.description: Cairns Customs House is a compact, two-storey building from the 1930s, set on Abbott Street, the main commercial street of the city centre. It was designed by Robert Henry Bowen and built in 1936-37 as a Depression-era job-creating project for the Australian Government. It was the third customs house on this site, which has been tied to the port of Cairns since the 1870s. The building is now a restaurant and sits inside the Reef Hotel Casino complex. It photographs well because it is a tidy, symmetrical piece of classical-style design. The entrance front has a projecting portico and balcony, tall double-height pilasters that rise to a stepped parapet, and timber shutters on the upper level. The rendered walls and terracotta tiled roof give you clean shapes and pale surfaces that a phone handles easily. Stand in front of the Abbott Street entrance, across the road from the portico, and you can fit the whole facade in one frame. Keep the phone level and use the gridlines so the pilasters stay upright. Then move closer for a tighter shot of the portico and parapet. If you want a second angle, the Esplanade side gives a longer street view toward the city, but check it on the spot, as it may not show the building clearly. The entrance area can be busy with people coming and going, so wait for a clear moment before you shoot.
text.geographic_location: It stands on Abbott Street at the southern end of Cairns city centre, with the Esplanade frontage behind it. The Reef Hotel Casino is built around it, and the Anzac Memorial Park is next door.
text.directions_text: Head for Abbott Street in the city centre and look for the Reef Hotel Casino; the Customs House is the small classical building at its front. No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so check a local map or journey planner for how to reach Abbott Street. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the whole facade. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if traffic or the kerb stops you stepping back, and to 2x or more for the parapet and pilasters.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Abbott Street (in front of the Abbott Street entrance facade, across the road from the portico). The classical Abbott Street front of the two-storey interwar building, with its projecting entrance portico, pilasters and stepped parapet.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up the pilasters with the vertical lines so the building does not lean. Put the portico in the centre and include the stepped parapet at the top. For a second shot, go closer and use 2x to fill the frame with the portico and shutters. The Esplanade offers a longer street view toward the city, but check on the spot whether it shows the building.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the pale walls to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the render keeps its detail and the sky does not wash out. Avoid ultra-wide close up, as it will stretch and tilt the building.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the walls than the middle of the day. Quieter times at the entrance make it easier to get a clear shot.

text.access_note: The building is a restaurant within the Reef Hotel Casino site, so you can photograph the front from the street, but check the official site before you go if you want to go inside.
